---
name: small-nodejs-service
description: 'Use when creating, reviewing, testing, or documenting backend or UI changes in this multi-tenant school portal, including services, auth roles, REST APIs, notifications, MongoDB references, and Vue UI calls.'
---

# Small Node.js Service

## Architecture

- Backend service modules live in `src/services/<service>/` and normally separate constants, router, controller, service, and database concerns. REST wrappers live in `src/services/rest/`.
- Public routes use `/api/v1`; service-to-service routes use `/api/internal_v1`. Use `RestCommsUtils` and the existing REST wrapper instead of calling another service's controller or database directly.
- A controller may call only the service owned by its microservice. Services must use the target microservice's `*Rest` wrapper for cross-service calls; do not import another microservice's service directly. Configure internal REST aliases for internal-only operations.
- Controllers adapt HTTP requests and responses. Joi validation and business orchestration belong in service modules. A service returns the real result: the real status and data on success (for example invite: `201` a new user, `200` a role added, `204` already a member, with the user) and a precise error (`403` exists but not reachable, `404` does not exist, `400` invalid). What a user is allowed to learn is decided in the controller, which faces the user: it normalizes the answer (the same status and body) when the difference would disclose something, so internal callers still know what happened. Mongo operations use `DbOpsUtils` and the shared database utilities.
- The Vue UI calls APIs through `ui/src/api/api.js`. Its Axios interceptor sends the HttpOnly cookie and selected `x-tenant-id`.
- `src/core` (utils, web-server) is a library that other applications can share: it never refers to this application. No `SMALL_API_*` / `SMALL_UI_*` setting, no service, role, school or other concept of the application, no test setup of the application. It receives what it needs as parameters (for example `WebServerUtils.init(..., settings)` with the CORS origins, the trusted proxies and the rate limits). The application reads its settings in `src/services/config.settings.js` (with their defaults) and in its services, and keeps its own code (and its test setup, `src/test/test-setup.utils.js`) out of the core.

## Routes and Naming

- A resource that gets a `PUT` route also gets the matching `PATCH` route (patch body `{ set, unset, add, remove }`), with the same role entries in `config.roles.json`.
- Name service and controller functions of public routes after the operation: `getOne`, `put`, `patch`, `putStatus`, `patchStatus`. Use the `ForReq` suffix only for functions that take `req` (like `getAllForReq(req, _ctx)`).
- Internal routes reached through `RestCommsUtils.put` / `RestCommsUtils.patch` with a field map to the local functions `put<Field>` / `patch<Field>` (for example `/:id/email` -> `putEmail`), so keep those names. When an internal route would share a name with a public one, give the internal function the `Internal` suffix (for example controller `getAllInternal`, service `getAllInternalForReq`). `putInternal` / `patchInternal` are the shared implementation helpers of a service, not routes.
- An action without a body (for example activating a user or a school) is an internal `POST /api/internal_v1/<service>/:id/<action>`. Its REST wrapper builds the config itself and calls `RestCommsUtils.call` with `localCall.fn` set to the action name.
- Keep `DbOpsUtils` generic: a condition goes in a generic option, never in a function made for one case. A conditional write uses `options.filter` of `DbOpsUtils.put` (one database call; `409` when the object exists but does not match, `404` when it does not exist), for example the activation (`{ status: 'pending' }`) or the status of a user that is not deleted; `deleteManyReferences` takes the same `options.filter` (the members that a group or a schedule does not list: `{ id: { $nin: ids } }`). `deleteAll` (a filter) refuses an empty filter. When a change (like a status) can come from several callers, give each caller its own route and service function with its own rules, and check where each one is called from.

## Tenant and Role Rules

- The selected tenant is `_ctx.tenantID`; tenant-scoped services should reject missing tenant context and rely on auth middleware to validate membership, active status, role, and route.
- `src/services/config.roles.json` is the route-to-role access matrix. Keep its routes synchronized with Express routers and service behavior.
- User roles are stored on each school membership. `admin`, `professor`, and `student` are school roles. `portal-admin` is an isolated role on the configured Portal School, not a synonym for school `admin`; do not grant both unless a specific requirement needs both.
- The portal school UUID is backend configuration (`SMALL_API_PORTAL_SCHOOL_ID`). Never embed it in UI source or UI environment variables. The UI derives portal permissions from the selected membership's returned roles.
- The Portal School is a tenant like the others: inviting a user to it gives `portal-admin`, and `portal-admin` can be given only there (enforced in `UsersAuthSignupService.invite`). It must remain active and is excluded from `GET /schools`; its admins are listed with the portal-admin-only `GET /users/portal-admins`. Keep those invariants enforced by backend services as well as the UI, which does not show the Portal School itself, only its admins.
- Routes shared between `portal-admin` and school roles (for example `POST /users-auth/invite`): the portal-admin check in `validatePortalAdminRoute` only grants access; anything else falls through to the normal school-role validation.
- Startup creates the Portal School record and, if `SMALL_API_PORTAL_ADMIN_EMAIL` is set and the Portal School has no portal admin, invites that email as the first `portal-admin` through the normal invite flow (`users-auth.setup.service.js`). Do not add anonymous self-promotion, initial passwords, or infer the role from school `admin`. Portal admins are listed with `GET /users/portal-admins` and removed with `PATCH /users-auth/school/user/:uid`. The bootstrap runs at every start and invites the configured email again while no portal admin is active (a pending one is invited again: a new setup link).
- `/users/:id` (`GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`) is scoped in the users service, not only by the route roles: the user itself sees and changes its own profile with all its schools, also without a school (the `self` role group of `config.roles.json`, checked before the school, for `:id` equal to the current user); a school admin reaches only members of the selected tenant and sees only that school in `schools`; a portal admin (on the Portal School) reaches any user, reads only id, name, email and status (not the schools or the personal profile fields), and changes only the name. Anything else answers `404`, so the existence of a user is not disclosed.
- Every event id (`<service>.<action>`, also `<action>.failed`) has a message in `src/translations/en.json`, under the lower-cased id; otherwise the id is shown as it is. A message uses only named placeholders: `{target}` (the target name), `{user}` (the user who did it) and the details of the event, from the event arguments object (`{school}`, `{reason}`, `{status}`, `{set.status}`); `{target}` and `{user}` win over a detail with the same name; no numbered placeholders (`{0}`); the placeholders are filled in one pass (`TranslationsUtils` `expandArgs`), so an inserted value is never expanded again; a failed event records its `reason`. Every string of `src/translations/en.json` is also in `ro.json`, with the same placeholders (checked by `translations.utils.files.test.js`). When you add an event, add its message (in both languages) and its id to the test "should have a message for every event of the services" (`events.service.translate.test.js`). Messages are translated when the event is stored.
- Events are stored per school (`events_<school id>`, read by the school admins with `GET /events`) and, for what belongs to no school (logins, password changes), in the global collection, read only by portal admins with `GET /events/global` (the Global Events page). Actions of anonymous requests are not recorded individually (only logged).
- The email of a user is its login and is changed only by the user, with the password (`/users-auth/id`). No admin route changes it.
- A portal admin removes a school admin with `DELETE /users/school-admins/:schoolId/:id` (`UsersService.deleteSchoolAdmin`): only the `admin` role on that school is removed and the user and its other roles are kept. All the admins of a school can be removed, the last one too: a school without an admin is allowed, because a portal admin can invite a new one at any time (do not add a last-admin check there). The same for the Portal School: a portal admin can remove another one and itself, and a portal without an active portal admin gets the configured one (`SMALL_API_PORTAL_ADMIN_EMAIL`) at the next start; do not keep a list or a count of the portal admins to prevent it. A school admin can remove the other admins of its school but not its own admin role (another admin or a portal admin removes it). School admins change roles in their own school with `PATCH /users-auth/school/user/:uid`, and that changes only the roles of the user in that school.
- Lists for portal admins (`GET /users`, `/users/portal-admins`, `/users/school-admins/:schoolId`) use the portal filter schema: no filter on the schools of the users, and a projection without them.
- Never trust a client-provided role or permission flag. Enforce access through the authenticated user record and route-role configuration.

## Service Patterns

- Validate request bodies and query filters with the service's Joi schemas. List routes use `RestApiUtils.buildFilterFromReq` and return `{ data, meta }`.
- After a schema validation, continue with the validated value (`objInfo = v.value`): it is converted and has no unknown keys. A date field is `Joi.string().isoDate()` (kept as an ISO string; `Joi.date()` would store a `Date`). An email uses `ValidationUtils.email()`, which normalizes it (NFKC, trimmed, lower case); an email that is not validated by a schema (a lookup, a token, a setting) goes through `ValidationUtils.normalizeEmail`. A service never changes an object of its caller (notifications are shared by several subscribers in one process).
- Service configuration declares references, projections, and notification payloads. Populate/expand references through `ReferencesUtils` and the corresponding `*Rest` service.
- Mutations generally follow validate, load config, populate references, translate, perform the database operation, raise an event, then raise a notification. Preserve rollback behavior for multi-step signup/invite flows.
- User invitations go through `UsersAuthSignupService.invite`: new users receive the signup/reset-password message; existing users receive the invite message. Every invitation (school roles and `portal-admin`) uses `UsersAuthRest.invite` / `POST /users-auth/invite` with the school taken from the selected tenant; do not add school-specific invite routes. A school admin invites any role of its own school, admins included (naming the selected school in `school.id` is the same invite). The one exception is a portal admin inviting the admin of another school: it names that school with `school.id` (only from the Portal School, only the `admin` role), and the same invite runs with the context of that school, as signup does for the first admin. The local-call mapping that exposes `signup` and `invite` on the users-auth local service is in `src/services/config.services.js`; the email sender is `UsersAuthService.sendInvite`.
- School creation stays in `UsersAuthSignupService.signup`, which creates the school through `SchoolsRest` and invites the first admin. Do not duplicate it with a public schools signup route or service.
- Fixed values (durations, names, cookie attributes, limits) are defined once in the owning service's constants file and used from there, never as literals in the code (for example `TokenExpiresIn.session * 1000`, not `12 * 60 * 60 * 1000`).
- Status and role transitions should follow the owning service constants. Do not duplicate literal status policy across controllers and UI when a constant/helper already exists.
- The status of a user is global (all its schools). `pending` is only the initial state: a user becomes `active` at its first login (internal `POST /users/:id/activate`) or is set `active` / `disabled` by a portal admin (`PUT|PATCH /users/:id/status`, one conditional write that never changes a `deleted` account), and never goes back to `pending`, except a deleted account created again by an invitation. The profile routes (`PUT|PATCH /users/:id`) refuse `status`. A portal admin cannot disable itself. `deleted`: the user deleted its account (see Accounts and members).
- The activation (`UsersService.activate`, `SchoolsService.activate`) reads the user or the school itself and changes only a `pending` one; an active or disabled one is returned unchanged, and the caller uses the returned status (a disabled user is refused at login, a disabled school stays disabled). Never decide on a membership copy or on a snapshot taken earlier in the flow.
- Do not nest calls: write one operation per statement and keep each result in a named variable (`const rService = await UsersService.getOne(...)` then `const r = Private.notDisclosed(rService, objID)`; `const message = await RestMessagesUtils.statusError(r.status, r.error, _ctx)` then `return res.status(r.status).json(message)`; `const corsMiddleware = cors(...)` then `app.use(corsMiddleware)`), never `f(await g(...))` or `h(i(...))` as an argument. This applies to the backend and the UI code. Not affected: the formatting inside log lines (`console.log(... JSON.stringify(CommonUtils.protectData(req.body)) ...)`), Joi schema definitions (`Joi.array().items(Joi.object().keys(...))`), and the tests.
- Add short section comments in the existing block-comment style when they explain a boundary or non-obvious invariant; add comments for the next statements, with clear explainations; add if it separates flows.

## Accounts and Members

- A user deletes its own account (`DELETE /users-auth`, `UsersRest.deleteAccount`): the users record is kept as a tombstone with the status `deleted` (id, name, email, `deletedTimestamp`), its memberships (`schools: []`) and its personal profile fields (`UsersConstants.ProfileFields`) are removed, its login is deleted and all its sessions and links are ended. A deleted account is refused at login and at every request (like a disabled one), even if a login was left by a failure. Users-auth removes the login of the users without an account (a modified user with the status `deleted`, a removed user that does not exist anymore) in its users notification handler, reading the users again, so a late notification never removes the login of an account created again.
- The records of a school (students, professors, admins) keep `status`: the status of the user while it has the role; `disabled` (the role was removed) or `deleted` (the account was deleted) when the record is kept as a trace, with `removedTimestamp`. A trace stays in the lists, the groups and the schedules, so the school knows what happened with the person. The school setting `settings.removedMembers` (`GET|PUT /schools/:id/settings`, the admins of that school only) decides: `keep` (the default: traces) or `delete` (the record is deleted, and its `removed` notification removes it from the groups and the schedules). The record of a user that never logged in (pending) is always deleted: an invitation that was not used leaves nothing. Deleting a trace (`DELETE /students/:id`, ...) deletes it for good.
- An invitation of a deleted user creates its account again (`UsersRest.recreateAccount`: `pending`, a new `createdTimestamp`, before its role is added): the roles given again make their traces members again (`active` or `pending`, the `restore` event), the others stay traces. A role is never added to a deleted account directly (`patchSchool` refuses it): only the invitation creates it again.
- A user without roles in any school logs in to the school selection, which says it is not a member of any school; it can still change its profile, its email and its password, and delete its account. A route without a school (`all`, `self`) uses the school of the request (`x-tenant-id`) only if the user is a member of it (`tenantVerified` of the validation); otherwise the middleware drops it, so nothing is written into another school (its events).
- Pending users and pending schools are removed `SMALL_API_PENDING_EXPIRES_IN` seconds (72 hours by default, as long as the setup link; `ConfigSettings.getPendingExpiresIn`) after their `createdTimestamp`, by a timer of the users and schools services (`PendingCleanupInterval`, every pod, `unref`); do not add a separate pending date. Not a MongoDB TTL index: it would delete without the events and the notifications. A pending portal admin expires too (a typo in the configured email leaves nothing; the next start invites the configured one while no portal admin is active); a recreated account that is not used in time is deleted again (its traces stay).

## Notifications

- A service keeps copies of the objects of other services and follows them through notifications (`config.services.js`: the subscriptions). Each service handles each source explicitly: `notification` validates, then a `switch` on `serviceName` calls a named handler (`onUsersNotification`, `onGroupsNotification`, ...) that says what is done and why; a source without copies is only logged (`ignored (no copy of it)`). Do not add a generic notification function in the base utils.
- A copy is updated only when it is older than the notified object (in `DbOpsUtils.updateManyReferences`, which returns the `ids` it updated, also in its `arrayFilters`): a copy of the same object (the same `createdTimestamp`) with a smaller or missing `modifiedCount`, or a copy of an object created again with the same id (another or no `createdTimestamp`, for example an account created again). A change that comes back through a cycle, or a late notification of an older change, changes nothing, so a cycle stops by itself. A reference projection always has `createdTimestamp` and `modifiedCount`, and so does a notification.
- Records written by an earlier version are completed at the end of the start, after the schools and the notifications are ready (`fillMissingStatus` of the admins, students and professors: the status of their user), school by school; a later start finds nothing to do. Do the same for a new field that the code needs on every record.
- A service whose copies changed notifies its changed objects again (only those), so the copies of the copies follow: a user changes its students and professors, a student changes its groups, a group changes its schedules, a class changes its schedules, which change their students, professors and groups. A group or a schedule that lists its members (`students`, `professors`, `groups`) is added to the listed members and removed from the others.
- Name variables and functions after the objects of the project (`students`, `groups`, `changedGroupsIDs`, `schoolClass`), never with generic words like `documents` or `items`. Keep the `console.log` lines of the flows and log each decision (a record deleted, kept as a trace, a notification ignored); never remove a log only to shorten the code.

## Security Rules

- Secrets come from the environment. In production the service refuses the example values of `src/.env.example`, weak values, and a `SMALL_API_S2SPASS` equal to an auth password (debug mode only warns). `JwtUtils` derives separate sign and encrypt keys from each password; never use a password directly as a key.
- The client address is `req.ip`, which follows `SMALL_API_TRUST_PROXY`; never read `x-forwarded-for` (or any identity header) directly.
- Rate limits (`rate-limiter.middleware.js`) count failed logins per account from one address and per account from all addresses (successful logins are not counted), and reset emails per account. They are per process.
- Every token has a purpose: a session token (`purpose: 'session'`, 12 h) is accepted only as the cookie, a reset token (`purpose`: `reset-password` 1 h, `signup` 72 h) only by the reset routes. Never put anything derived from a password (not even a hash) in a token.
- Sessions and emailed links are records of `users-auth.sessions.service.js`, in their own collection (`users-auth-sessions`). A token carries a random secret (32 bytes); the record keeps only its SHA-256 hash (the record id), the user, the purpose and `expiresAt` (a TTL index removes the expired records). Every use checks the record (`check`). A session also ends after `SessionLimits.IdleTimeout` without requests; its `lastUsedAt` is saved at most every `SessionLimits.TouchInterval`, so most requests only read (never save it on every request). A new session ends the oldest sessions of the user over `SessionLimits.MaxPerUser`. Logout ends its own session (`end`), a link is used once (`end`, a `404` means it was already used) and a newer link replaces the older ones; a password change (the current session continues with a new one), a password reset, an email change and a removed account end all the records of the user (`endAll`). Never keep session state on the account (the `users-auth` document), and never add a way to change a password or an email that does not call `endAll`.
- An emailed link points to the UI (`SMALL_UI_URL`, page `/reset-password`) with the token in the URL fragment; the page sends it in the `x-reset-token` header. A token is never put in a query string.
- The auth cookie is set and cleared with `cookieOptions` (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite` from `SMALL_API_COOKIE_SAMESITE`, `Secure` outside debug mode); its attributes are `AuthCookie` and its lifetime is `TokenExpiresIn.session` (seconds), both in `users-auth.constants.js`.
- Internal routes (`/api/internal_v1`) answer `404` unless `SMALL_API_INTERNAL_ROUTES=true` (services in separate processes). A service token is bound to the method and path, valid for 60 s, and used once (`jti`).
- Public answers never tell if an account exists, and this is done in the controllers: reset password answers `200` for an unknown address, invite answers `200 { username, type }` (signup `201 { username, type }`) for new users, existing users and members alike, every failed login answers `401 Invalid username/password` (a server error stays `5xx`), and `/users/:id` answers `404` for a user of another school as for a missing one. The services return the real result; the local login also hashes the password for a missing account (constant-time comparison), so the time does not tell either.
- A failed login is only logged (reason, never the password), not recorded as an event: anybody can cause many. Record events for what authenticated users change.
- Error answers come from `RestMessagesUtils.statusError` (controllers, middlewares, and the error middleware for what no controller answers): `{ message }` with the generic text of the status. A `400` also has `detail`, the message the service wrote, in every mode, so the user knows what to change: write it for people, about the request itself, never with an internal address, a stack, or data of another account. `401`, `403`, `404` and `5xx` never carry a reason (the reason could tell if an account exists, and a server error never shows its cause); debug mode adds `error`. A REST call between services keeps the callee's `detail` of a `400` as its message, never the address of the call.

## UI Patterns

- Derive page/menu permissions with `getRolesPermissions` from the selected active school membership. Also protect privileged routes with the router guard; backend checks remain authoritative.
- Reuse the `ApiTableServer` and `ComponentsUtils.Edit` patterns for CRUD pages. A "more info" panel (the expanded row of a page's table) is compact like the other pages: a `v-card` with `v-card-text`, a right-aligned `v-col cols="12" md="10"`, and the dense `ApiTableData` (directly, or through `ApiFieldDetails` / the `api.references.*` components) with the items loaded by the panel; do not nest a full `ApiTableServer` (toolbar, paging) in it. Use existing invite flows for user-backed records rather than making duplicate user-creation endpoints.
- Keep API methods in `ui/src/api/api.js` and use translations from `ui/src/translations/` for visible labels.
- Show a text translated by the server (`_lang_<language>` copies: message, severity, frequency) with `ComponentUtils.getServerText(item, path, locale)`, in the language of the UI with English as fallback, and request the copies with `ComponentUtils.getServerLanguages(locale)` in the projection.
- Show a status with the UI translations (`ComponentUtils.getStatusText`, the same keys as the edit dialogs), not with the label translated by the server (`_lang_en`), which is always English; the server label is only a fallback for a value the UI does not know.
- Calls started by the user run one at a time: `ComponentsUtils.useSingleCall()` gives a reactive `{ inProgress, loading, itemID, run }` (an instance per action, named after it: `saveCall`, `loginCall`; the handler is `await saveCall.run(submit, itemID)`), and `ComponentsUtils.useItemCalls()` one call per row (`deleteCalls.run(itemID, fn)`, `isInProgress(itemID)`, `isLoading(itemID)`). `run` marks the call in progress before the first `await` (the form validation included), so a second click or Enter sends nothing. Name these helpers and their instances after calls (the word the project uses for a request), never with vague words like `busy`.
- A dialog closes when its call starts and is not shown again: its own rules check the input before, and the snackbar tells the result, a refusal too. The button that opened it shows the call instead: the `+` of a table, the edit or delete icon of a row, a button of the profile is disabled while the call is in progress, with the spinner. A table takes the call of its page as `call` (its `itemID` is the row of an edit, `null` the `+`) and runs its deletes with `useItemCalls`; a dialog component (`ApiUserEditDialog`, `PasswordChange`, `EmailChange`) takes the call of its parent as `call`; the row icons are `ActionIcon` (`base.action.icon.vue`). While the call is in progress the buttons that open its dialog do nothing, and the dialog's form is cleared when it closes. Only a page (login, set password) or a dialog that shows the answer itself ("Forgot password?") stays in place, with the spinner on its own button.
- A spinner or a loader is shown only when the call takes longer than `ComponentsUtils.LoadingDelay` (300 ms): `loading` of `useSingleCall` / `useItemCalls`, and the loader of a list or of details (a `LoadingDelay` timer, cleared at the answer). A fast call shows nothing, so the screen does not flicker.
- Only the latest answer is shown: a component that loads a list or the details of an item numbers its calls with `ComponentsUtils.useLatestCall()` and drops an answer (and its error, and the end of its loader) that is not the latest one; the details also drop an answer for an item that is not the open one, and clear the previous item at once (`ApiDetails` emits `item` with `null`). A filter that loads from the server waits for a pause in typing (`FilterDelay`). A details panel replaces its details (`itemDetails.value = { ...data }`), never merges them into the old ones.
- Show a failed request with `ComponentsUtils.getErrorText(e, t)`: the `detail` of a `400`, otherwise the translated text of the status (`error.status.<status>`), or `error.network` when there is no answer; never `e.response.data.error` (only in debug mode) or `e.toString()`. An invite says `invite.success` (its answer is the same for a new user, an existing user and a member, on purpose).
- Every page after the login has the header of the app (`base.layout.vue`) with the user menu, so the user can always log out. The school selection (`/tenants`, route meta `noMenu`) has the header without the menu of the pages and the breadcrumbs (no school is chosen yet), and says so when the user is not a member of any school, with a link to the profile. The profile (route meta `noTenant`) opens also without a school (then without the menu of the pages); the user menu always offers it. Only the pages without a session (login, set password; meta `noLayout`) have no header.
- Delete buttons are hidden until the user asks for them, so nothing is deleted by an accidental click (a delete is also confirmed): `ShowDelete` (`base.show.delete.vue`, "Show delete" / "Hide delete") is in the header of the actions column of a table with a header, next to the "+" of a list without a header (the inner lists of the "more info" panels), and in the toolbar of the profile (its "Delete my account"). A custom actions slot gets `showDelete` from the table and uses it for its delete icon.
- A settings page shows each setting on one line: its name and its current choice, with an edit icon that opens a dialog where the choice is made (each option explained there); a choice that can not be undone is confirmed.
- The Admins, Students and Professors pages (and the lists of the students and professors of a group or a schedule) show the status of the record (`status`: also `disabled` and `deleted` for a trace), not the status of the user; they edit only the name of a person, never its status. The Settings page (`/settings`, permission `settings`, school admins) has the line of the removed members; its dialog explains the two choices, and the `delete` choice is confirmed (it can not be undone). The profile has "Delete my account" (shown with "Show delete"), confirmed, then the stores are cleared and the login is shown. Portal admins edit users (name and status) with the shared `ApiUserEditDialog` (`api.user.edit.dialog.vue`), which calls the profile route for the name and the status route for the status, and hides the status for the current user. It is used by the Users page (`/users`, permission `users`), the portal admins list, and the admins of a school on the Schools page.

## Dependencies

- Versions are pinned exactly in `package.json`, and both `src/package-lock.json` and `ui/package-lock.json` are committed; install with `npm ci`. After a change of a dependency, commit the updated lockfile.
- A dependency is declared only if the code uses it; remove the unused ones.
- The CI (`.github/workflows/dependencies.yml`) refuses production dependencies with an advisory of high or critical severity (`npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`), on every change and every week. Fix an advisory by upgrading within the major version; a major upgrade is a change of its own, with its tests.
- The UI loads no code or style from a CDN: everything is bundled from `node_modules` (icons with `@mdi/font`). A third-party resource that can not be bundled needs `integrity` and `crossorigin`.
- Use libraries as documented, not by accident (for example `jwt.verify(..., { algorithms: ['HS512'] })` takes a list).

## Tests

- Service tests live in `src/test/test/<service>/`, use Sinon stubs, and are registered by the service's `*.all.tests.js` file. Add tests for success, validation, dependency failures, and authorization/invariants appropriate to the change.
- Auth route behavior belongs in `users-auth.service.validate.test.js`; public controller behavior belongs in the owning controller test suite.
- Run a focused Mocha file or suite first (with `--require test/hooks.js --exit`). The backend's complete unit suite is `cd src && npm test`; the functional tests with the database (`src/test/test/functional/`, including the flows of the accounts in `functional.users-auth.test.js`) run with `npm run testdb` and need the MongoDB of `SMALL_API_DATABASE_URL`. When functional tests fail, compare with the same run on the base commit before concluding that a change caused it, then fix them (do not leave them failing).
- The tests do not depend on the machine: `TestUtils.setupEnv` (`src/test/test-setup.utils.js`) removes every `SMALL_API_*` / `SMALL_UI_*` setting of the shell and sets the test values, and a test that needs another value sets it and restores it. The stubs of the start (the database, the mail, the portal school) are set when `src/test/hooks.js` is loaded, before any test file starts the service, and the hooks wait for the start (`index.js` `initialized`). The unit tests never connect to a database or a mail server: a test that runs the init of the services stubs the `init` of the databases, and a test that loops over many schools stubs the `collection` of their database. `npm run testdb` drops its test database (`TestConstants.Database.Db`) at the start, so nothing of an earlier run or version is left. A stub of `UsersAuthRest.validate` answers like the validation of a member (`tenantVerified: true`), and a stub of `RestCommsUtils.restValidation` sets the user of the call like a service token.
- `TestUtils.setupEnv` enables the internal routes and uses test-only secrets; the salt stays the example one because the stored password hashes of the test users depend on it. A test that runs `initEnv` as production must give strong secrets, or it exits.
- Test data uses normal, realistic values (names, emails on `testdomain.test`, ids), not words like `evil` or `attacker`, even in security tests.
- Every test (`it`) has a block comment right above it (`/** ... */`, one short line that says what it shows), so the tests are easy to spot in the editor; also an `it` inside a loop. Inside the test, a `//` comment starts each important step: the stubs (`// stub: ...`), the call (`// call ...`), the checks (`// check: ...`), and each case of a test that checks several cases in turn. Say what the step means (`// stub: no stored user; no write is expected`), not only its name.
- Format only the files that were changed (`npx prettier --write <files>`), and check the diff: if the formatter changes lines that were not part of the change, restore the file and re-apply only the change.
- UI scripts are in `ui/package.json`; validate Vue changes with `npm run build` if the lint command is unavailable.
